parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, border, facility, custody or care restriction is documented; same-sex conduct is lawful and anti-discrimination cover for gender identity exists on paper. If outed, the documented consequences are primarily harassment, discrimination and Pride-scoped violence, not state detention or severe punishment. Weak, vague enforcement, untracked incident recording, heteronormative generic victim services, and NGO-described prevalent under-reported violence lower confidence and recourse, placing this well below functioning-protection systems but above jurisdictions with universal exposure or targeting.

entry_documents.protection: No documented border or document-mismatch sanction; legal gender recognition exists for residents as a climate signal only, not a visitor protection.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented interaction between visitor documents and border screening in the dossier.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No subnational facility regime is documented; the only documented variation concerns residents' local gender-recognition procedure, not visitor facilities.

care_services.protection: Medical treatment is not required for residents' legal gender recognition, a climate signal only; visitor care access is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2016 anti-discrimination law and 2003 education rules described as vague, open to interpretation and very rarely enforced.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation since 2016 expressly covering gender identity; same-sex relations lawful nationwide and LGBTIQ organisations may register.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Favourable paper law interacts with weak enforcement, so protection is limited in practice without any documented hostile state policy.

minors_guardians.protection: Education discrimination rules since 2003 are resident-facing and rarely enforced; no visitor-specific minor rule is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: No documented age-dependent visitor exposure; general discrimination protections are the only relevant signal.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: June 2023 Pride: threats, insults, flag burnings, property destruction, eggs thrown, woman assaulted, two people assaulted with minor injuries; NGOs describe violence as prevalent and under-reported.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police received reports and investigated attacks and disturbances; head of state attended Pride and ombudsman, legislature president, head of state and later head of government condemned violence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence was capital-event-scoped in the record, while authorities log incidents without tracking case numbers, limiting follow-up despite the investigation and condemnations.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Institutional shortcomings in the hate-crime framework; generic victim services present heteronormative hurdles; raw 17 and 25 incident counts lack denominator and coverage.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil society provides counselling, advocacy and safe spaces; official investigations and condemnations occurred after Pride.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Civil-society recourse partly offsets weak state enforcement, but delayed government reaction and silence from interior minister show uneven institutional response.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.65-D in that Pride-related harassment and brief violence occurred while some oversight and condemnation existed, but lower here because documented enforcement of protections is very rare and incident tracking is absent, whereas that anchor showed effective judicial dismissal and a misconduct finding.

Similar to 0.75-D overall: paper equality protections, possible physical attacks in visible settings, and imperfect remedies, but no documented visitor detention or facility ban; here remedy quality is less proven, so slightly below that anchor's clearer police-review and prosecution pathway.

Materially below 0.85-A because that anchor documents independent investigation, discipline, compensation and functioning courts, whereas this dossier documents vague rarely-enforced law, untracked cases and reliance on civil society for victim support.

parsed.synthesis: The combined national regime contains no documented universal-exposure measure, organised targeting, criminalisation or custody risk for a visitor, so severity after outing is mainly social hostility, discrimination and event-scoped violence. Favourable law and official condemnation are real positives, but they are diluted by weak enforcement, untracked recording, uneven ministerial response and victim support concentrated in civil society. That combination supports Reduced Risk, below systems where remedies demonstrably work, and well above any system imposing state exclusion or detention.
